mainTopic: Which blood is forbidden: human blood, heart blood, bloodletting life-blood and דם התמצית; then a doubt of מעילה and the אשם תלוי
overview: This amud first finishes the discussion of human blood. Blood that has left the body (פירש) is forbidden, but blood still in the body, like blood between the teeth, is permitted. A second version places רב ששת's statement, that there is not even a מצוה to stay away from human blood, on a ברייתא that uses the פסוק "וזה לכם הטמא" to permit human milk and blood. Next, רב says that the blood inside an animal's heart brings כרת. The גמרא defends this by separating the heart's own soaked-in blood from blood the dying heart pulls in from the body. רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש then argue about which bloodletting blood counts as life-blood: only spurting blood, or all red blood from the black drop onward. Their argument turns out to match a disagreement between תנאים, and it decides the case of blood caught in two cups. רבי יהודה makes a person liable for דם התמצית, but he agrees it cannot bring כפרה, as a ברייתא in the ספרא shows. Finally, a new משנה brings the argument of רבי עקיבא, the חכמים and רבי טרפון about an אשם תלוי for a doubt of מעילה.

steps.title: Separated blood versus blood that never left the body
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes its answer. The source that forbids human blood is talking about blood that left the body. רב ששת, who permits it completely, is talking about blood that never left the body.
steps.simpleTranslation: The source that forbids it speaks of blood that separated from the person. When רב ששת said it is fully permitted, he meant blood that did not separate.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing an answer to an earlier challenge against רב ששת by splitting human blood into two cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before this, a source seemed to forbid human blood, which went against רב ששת. The answer is that the two sources are talking about different blood. Blood that left the body (פירש) is forbidden by the רבנן, but blood still connected to the person (לא פירש) is completely permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: Separated: the blood has left the person's body
Did not separate: blood still in or attached to the person
When he said: this tells us what case the speaker meant

steps.confusionAlert: This is not saying human blood is a Torah prohibition when it separates. Human blood is never forbidden by the Torah. The issue is only the extra rabbinic restriction on blood that has left the body.

phrases.english: where it separated.
phrases.notes: This finishes the sentence from before: the source that forbids human blood is talking about blood that already left the body.

phrases.english: When Rav said
phrases.notes: He means רב ששת, whose ruling is being defended here.

phrases.english: it was where it did not separate,

steps.terutzMaskana: Separated blood is forbidden. Blood that never left the body is fully permitted.

steps.title: Support from blood on bread and between the teeth
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows the difference in practice. Blood on bread has left the body, so you scrape it off. Blood between your teeth is still in your body, so you may swallow it.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: if blood is on a loaf of bread, you scrape it off and eat the bread. If blood is between your teeth, you may suck it and swallow it without worry.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to support the split it just made.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Blood on bread has left the body (פירש), so it must be scraped off. Blood between the teeth has not left the body (לא פירש), so it may be swallowed. This matches exactly the line drawn in step 1.

keyTerms.meaning: A loaf of bread
He scrapes it off
He sucks and swallows
He need not worry

steps.whatToRemember: Human blood that left the body is forbidden by the רבנן, so scrape it off the bread. Blood still in the mouth, between the teeth, is permitted.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the practical rule people actually use, for example when their gums bleed.

he scrapes it off and eats it,
phrases.notes: He scrapes off the blood and then eats the bread.

phrases.english: blood that is between the teeth,

steps.title: Second version: a logical case to forbid human milk
steps.stepSummary: Some place רב ששת's statement on a different ברייתא. That ברייתא starts by suggesting a קל וחומר that would forbid human milk.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some teach רב ששת's statement on this ברייתא. One might think that someone who drinks the milk of two-legged creatures breaks a לאו. Here is the reasoning. A non-kosher animal does not make things impure by touch while alive, yet its milk is forbidden. Humans do make things impure by touch, so shouldn't their milk surely be forbidden?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a second version of where רב ששת's statement belongs. It starts quoting a ברייתא, which first suggests a קל וחומר that it will soon reject.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The קל וחומר works like this. A בהמה טמאה is treated leniently for touch, because a live animal does not transmit impurity, but strictly for milk. Humans are treated strictly for touch, since living people can transmit impurity, so we would expect them to be strict for milk too. This is a הוה אמינא that the ברייתא is setting up to knock down.

keyTerms.meaning: Some teach it: brings in a second version of where a statement belongs
One might have thought: introduces an idea that will be rejected
Those that walk on two legs: humans
And it is logical: introduces a קל וחומר
Touch: passing on impurity by contact
A non-kosher animal

steps.confusionAlert: Here חלב means milk, not forbidden fat. The ברייתא is asking about drinking human milk.

phrases.english: There are those who teach it

steps.title: The פסוק permits human milk
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק "וזה לכם הטמא" limits the impure list to the creatures named there, so human milk is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: "And these are impure to you." These are impure, but the milk of humans is not impure. It is pure.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא rejects the קל וחומר from step 3 by quoting a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word "זה" (this) limits the impure status to the creatures listed in the פסוק. Humans are not on that list, so their milk is permitted. A clear פסוק beats a logical argument.

keyTerms.meaning: The פסוק teaches: brings a verse to settle the question
This: a limiting word that leaves out anything not listed
Pure; here it means permitted to eat

phrases.english: The verse states: "And these are impure to you"
this is impure,
but the milk of two-legged creatures is not impure
but rather pure.

steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole קל וחומר to forbid human milk
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A פסוק excludes human milk, so the logic cannot stand

steps.title: Maybe human blood is still forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא pushes back. Milk is different, because not all milk is forbidden. But all blood is forbidden, so maybe human blood is forbidden too.
steps.simpleTranslation: I should leave out milk from the prohibition, since milk is not forbidden in all cases. But I should not leave out blood, which is forbidden in all cases!
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא raises a new challenge: the פסוק may permit human milk, but perhaps human blood is still forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Milk is not forbidden across the board, since kosher animals' milk is permitted, so leaving out human milk is easy. Blood is forbidden in all creatures, even kosher ones. So we might think human blood stays forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: I will leave out: exclude from the rule
The same for all: applies to every kind of creature
Milk (here, not forbidden fat)

phrases.aramaic: אוֹצִיא אֶת הֶחָלָב, שֶׁאֵין שָׁוֶה בַּכֹּל,
phrases.english: I will exclude the milk, which is not the same for all,
phrases.notes: Kosher animals' milk is permitted, so the milk prohibition does not apply to every creature.

phrases.english: but I will not exclude the blood, which is the same for all!

steps.triggerLanguage: אוֹצִיא אֶת הֶחָלָב שֶׁאֵין שָׁוֶה בַּכֹּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Argues that the exclusion in step 4 should stop at milk
steps.kashyaTarget: Using the exclusion from "וזה לכם הטמא" for blood too
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Blood is forbidden in every creature, unlike milk, so it may not be covered by the same exclusion

steps.title: The same פסוק permits human blood
steps.stepSummary: The same פסוק, "וזה לכם הטמא", also excludes human blood.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: "And these are impure to you." These are impure, but the blood of humans is not impure. It is pure.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers the challenge by using the same פסוק to permit human blood as well.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even though blood is forbidden in all creatures, the word "זה" still leaves humans out. So by Torah law, human blood is not forbidden at all.

keyTerms.meaning: Blood of two-legged creatures: human blood
"And these are impure to you": the פסוק used for both exclusions
An exclusion learned from a limiting word in a פסוק

phrases.english: The verse states: "And these are impure to you"
this is impure,
but the blood of two-legged creatures is not impure

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 5
steps.terutzResolutionType: The same פסוק covers blood too
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Human blood stays forbidden because blood is forbidden in all creatures
steps.terutzMaskana: Human blood is not forbidden by the Torah

steps.title: רב ששת: not even a מצוה to stay away
steps.stepSummary: In this version, רב ששת adds to the ברייתא that with human blood there is not even a מצוה to keep away from it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said: there is not even a מצוה to stay away from it.
steps.whatsHappening: In the second version, רב ששת comments on the ברייתא: human blood is so permitted that there is not even a מצוה to avoid it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא only said human blood is not forbidden by the Torah. רב ששת goes further: there is no lower-level מצוה to stay away from it either. In this version his statement is attached to the ברייתא's ruling about human blood, not to the case of blood that never left the body.

keyTerms.meaning: A מצוה to stay away: a lower-level duty to avoid something
Even
From the start: the ideal way to act

steps.whatToRemember: Both versions agree that human blood is not forbidden by the Torah. The first version limits רב ששת's full permission to blood that never left the body. The second version puts his statement on the ברייתא that permits human blood in general.

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said:
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets and some leave it out. It does not change the meaning.

phrases.english: there is not even a command to abstain from it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת אֲפִילּוּ מִצְוַת פְּרוֹשׁ אֵין בּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Places רב ששת's statement on the ברייתא's final ruling about human blood
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Human blood carries not even a מצוה to stay away from it

steps.title: The משנה about tearing the heart
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה from חולין: tear the heart to remove its blood, but if you did not, you have not broken the prohibition.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in a משנה elsewhere: a heart must be torn open and its blood taken out. If he did not tear it, he does not break the prohibition.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic by quoting a משנה from another מסכת about the blood inside a heart. This sets up רב's comment in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says two things. First, you should tear the heart and drain its blood before eating. Second, if you skipped this and ate it, you did not break the prohibition of eating blood. The question that follows is why eating that blood is not a violation.

keyTerms.meaning: He tears it open
He does not break the prohibition
Heart

phrases.english: We learned there:
phrases.notes: This is a משנה in חולין, not our מסכת.

phrases.english: The heart: he tears it and takes out its blood;
if he did not tear it, he does not break the prohibition.

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנַן הָתָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, moving from human blood to the blood of the heart.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A heart should be torn to remove its blood, but if it was not torn, there is no violation.

steps.title: רב limits the משנה to a bird's heart
steps.stepSummary: רב says the משנה only means a bird's heart, which holds less than a כזית of blood. An animal's heart holds a כזית, so eating it brings כרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said in the name of רב: this was taught only about a bird's heart, since it does not hold a כזית. But an animal's heart, which holds a כזית, is forbidden and brings כרת.
steps.whatsHappening: רב explains why the משנה said there is no violation. It is talking only about a small bird's heart.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Punishment for eating blood requires a כזית. A bird's heart is too small to hold that much blood, so there is no punishable violation. An animal's heart is big enough, so eating its blood brings full כרת.

keyTerms.meaning: They taught this only about...
An olive's volume, the minimum amount for punishment
Spiritual cutting off, the punishment for eating blood
Since, because

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the הלכה that blood inside an animal's heart is real blood that brings כרת, which the rest of the סוגיא defends.

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said that Rav said:
They taught this only about a bird's heart,
since it does not have an olive's volume of blood in it;

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל לֵב בְּהֵמָה דְּיֵשׁ בּוֹ כְּזַיִת –
phrases.english: but an animal's heart, which does have an olive's volume in it,
is forbidden, and one is liable to כרת for it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא אָמַר רַב לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the משנה from step 8 to a bird's heart.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Blood in an animal's heart is a כזית and brings כרת. The משנה's leniency is only for a bird's heart.

steps.title: A ברייתא says heart blood is only a לא תעשה
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא lists heart blood with blood that is only a regular לא תעשה, not כרת. This seems to contradict רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged: blood of the spleen, of the heart, of the kidneys, and of the limbs are all under a לא תעשה. Blood of two-legged creatures and of bugs and crawling creatures is forbidden, but one is not liable for it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב with a ברייתא that puts heart blood in the lighter group, with no כרת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב said an animal's heart blood brings כרת. The ברייתא says heart blood is only a regular לא תעשה. So the ברייתא seems to argue with רב.

keyTerms.meaning: A negative commandment, here punished with lashes, not כרת
Blood soaked into the limbs and organs
Two-legged walkers, meaning people
Bugs and crawling creatures

phrases.english: They challenged: blood of the spleen, blood of the heart,
blood of the kidneys, blood of the limbs,
these are under a negative commandment.
Blood of two-legged creatures,
blood of bugs and crawling creatures,
is forbidden, but one is not liable for it!

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵיתִיבִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב's ruling from step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling that an animal's heart blood brings כרת.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא puts heart blood in the list of blood that is only a לא תעשה, so it does not bring כרת.

steps.title: The heart's own blood versus blood from outside
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא means blood soaked into the heart itself. רב means blood that flowed into the heart from the rest of the body.
steps.simpleTranslation: When the ברייתא teaches 'not liable', it means the heart's own blood. When רב spoke, he meant blood that comes into it from elsewhere.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא and רב are talking about two different kinds of blood in the heart.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Blood soaked into the heart's walls is only a לא תעשה, like the ברייתא says. Blood collected inside the heart came from the whole body, so it is regular blood that brings כרת. That is רב's case.

keyTerms.meaning: Its own blood, soaked into the heart itself
That comes to it from outside, from the rest of the body

phrases.english: When it teaches 'one is not liable for it,'
phrases.notes: He means not liable to כרת.

phrases.english: that is about its own blood;
when רב spoke,
it was about blood that comes into it from outside.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי קָתָנֵי אֵין חַיָּיבִין עָלָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: two different kinds of blood in the heart.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא and רב seemed to be talking about the same heart blood.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא means blood soaked into the heart's walls. רב means blood inside the heart that came from the body.

steps.title: The heart's own blood is already blood of limbs
steps.stepSummary: If the ברייתא means the heart's own blood, that is just 'blood of limbs', which the list already has. Why mention it twice?
steps.simpleTranslation: Its own blood is the same as blood of limbs!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer. The heart's own blood is already covered by 'blood of limbs' in the same list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא lists both 'blood of the heart' and 'blood of limbs'. If heart blood means the blood soaked into the heart, it is no different from blood soaked into any limb. So listing it separately looks extra.

keyTerms.meaning: That is the same as

phrases.english: Its own blood is the same as blood of limbs!

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּם דִּילֵיהּ הַיְינוּ דַּם אֵבָרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer in step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the ברייתא's 'blood of the heart' means its own absorbed blood.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Then 'blood of the heart' would repeat 'blood of limbs', and a ברייתא should not repeat itself.

steps.title: The same overlap exists with the kidneys
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers back: the ברייתא also lists kidney blood next to limb blood, so the same overlap happens anyway.
steps.simpleTranslation: And by your reasoning, doesn't it teach blood of the kidneys and also teach blood of the limbs?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes the question away by showing the same 'problem' shows up elsewhere in the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Kidney blood is also blood soaked into an organ, yet the ברייתא lists it separately from blood of limbs. So the overlap cannot be a real objection. It must be the ברייתא's normal style.

keyTerms.meaning: And according to your reasoning, a counter-question
Doesn't it teach?

phrases.english: And by your reasoning,
doesn't it teach blood of the kidneys
and also teach blood of the limbs?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלִיטַעְמָיךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the challenge in step 12 back on the questioner.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The claim that the heart's own blood cannot be listed separately from blood of limbs.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The same overlap exists with kidney blood, so overlap alone proves nothing.

steps.title: A specific case first, then the general rule
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא names a specific organ and then gives the general rule. The heart works the same way.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it teaches one thing and then teaches again. Here too, it teaches one thing and then teaches again.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא ends the discussion. The ברייתא lists specific organs and then sums up with 'blood of limbs', so listing the heart is fine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא's style is to name specific organs like the kidneys and the heart, and then add the general category of limbs. So 'blood of the heart' really can mean its own blood, and the גמרא's answer in step 11, which defends רב, stands.

keyTerms.meaning: It teaches, then teaches again: a specific case, then a general rule
Here too

steps.whatToRemember: Blood soaked into the heart is only a לא תעשה. Blood collected inside an animal's heart came from the body and brings כרת. The ברייתא's list names specific organs and then adds the general 'blood of limbs'.

phrases.english: Rather, it teaches and then teaches again;
here too, it teaches and then teaches again.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא תָּנֵי וַהֲדַר תָּנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the point of step 13 and settles the challenge in step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explaining the ברייתא's style: specific case first, then general rule.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Listing heart blood next to limb blood seemed like a needless repeat.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא often names a specific organ and then the general category, so the answer in step 11 holds.

steps.title: How does outside blood get into the heart?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how blood from the rest of the body ends up inside the heart, as רב's case assumes.
steps.simpleTranslation: From outside, where does the heart get this blood from?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a practical question about רב's case: how does blood from the rest of the body actually get into the heart?
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 11, the גמרא said רב means blood that flowed into the heart from elsewhere. That only works if outside blood really can reach the heart, so the גמרא wants to know how that happens.

keyTerms.meaning: From outside, from elsewhere in the body
From where does it come to it?

phrases.english: From outside, from where does it come to it?
phrases.notes: 'It' here is the heart. The גמרא is asking about רב's case of blood that came into the heart from the body.

steps.triggerLanguage: מעלמא מהיכא אתי ליה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows up on the definition of רב's case given in Step 11, after the side discussion in Steps 12-14.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The physical way outside blood enters the heart, which רב's case depends on.

steps.title: The dying heart pulls blood in
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא explains that when the animal is dying, the heart draws blood in from the body.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said: At the moment the soul leaves, the heart pulls blood in strongly.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא answers the question: as the animal dies, the heart sucks blood in from the rest of the body.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This shows that רב's case can really happen. The blood pulled in at death is blood from the body itself, so it carries כרת. That is different from the heart's own soaked-in blood in the ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: At the time the soul leaves, the moment of death
It surely draws in, it sucks in strongly

steps.whatToRemember: רב's heart blood is blood the dying heart pulls in from the body. It counts as real blood that carries כרת.

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said:
At the time when the soul departs,
it surely draws [blood in].

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר רבי זירא בשעה שהנשמה יוצאה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the question of Step 15.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: At death the heart pulls blood in from the body, so רב's case is real.

steps.title: The משנה's rule on blood with which the soul departs
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: blood with which the soul leaves carries liability.
steps.simpleTranslation: Blood with which the soul goes out: one is liable for it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic by quoting a line from the משנה. This sets up the question that comes next: which blood exactly is this?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה makes a person liable (כרת if done on purpose, a חטאת if by mistake) for blood 'with which the soul departs.' It does not say exactly which part of the blood flow this is, so the next step will define it.

keyTerms.meaning: Blood with which the soul departs, the life-blood
One is liable for it (כרת or a חטאת)

phrases.english: Blood with which the soul departs –
one is liable for it.

steps.triggerLanguage: דם שהנשמה יוצאה בו חייבין עליו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the heart-blood topic and opens a new section based on the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Eating blood with which the soul departs makes one liable.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש define bloodletting life-blood
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says only blood that spurts forcefully counts. ריש לקיש says it counts from right after the black drops.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: Which bloodletting blood is the blood that the soul depends on? רבי יוחנן says: as long as it spurts. ריש לקיש says: from the black drop and onward.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים argue about which part of the bloodletting flow counts as life-blood that carries כרת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When an animal is bled, black drops come out first. Then red blood comes, spurts strongly, and finally just trickles. רבי יוחנן counts only the strong spurt. ריש לקיש counts all the red blood from right after the black drops, even before and after the spurt.

keyTerms.meaning: Blood of bloodletting, blood let from a cut vein
Depends on it
Spurts out forcefully in a stream
The blackish drop that comes out first

steps.confusionAlert: ריש לקיש does not count the black drops themselves. He counts the red blood that comes after them, even if it is not spurting yet.

phrases.english: It was stated: What is the blood of bloodletting
upon which the soul depends?
Rabbi Yoḥanan says:
As long as it is spurting.
Reish Lakish says:
From the black drop and onward.
phrases.notes: He means once the dark first drops are over, the red blood after them already counts, even before it spurts.

steps.triggerLanguage: איתמר איזהו דם הקזה שהנשמה תלויה בו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines the משנה's term quoted in Step 17.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוחנן: only spurting blood carries כרת. ריש לקיש: all red blood after the black drops carries כרת.

steps.title: A ברייתא seems to refute ריש לקיש
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says only spurting blood counts and trickling blood is excluded. That seems to exclude the first and last red blood, against ריש לקיש.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged from a ברייתא: Which bloodletting blood is the blood the soul leaves with? As long as it spurts. This leaves out the trickling-out blood, because it only flows. Doesn't that mean the first and last blood too, since it only flows, counts like trickling blood? This is a refutation of ריש לקיש!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that sounds just like רבי יוחנן, and argues it disproves ריש לקיש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא excludes דם התמצית because it only flows and does not spurt. The גמרא reasons that the reason 'it only flows' should also apply to the first and last red blood. So the ברייתא seems to exclude blood that ריש לקיש counts.

keyTerms.meaning: Trickling blood that oozes out at the end, after the spurt
Flowing or dripping slowly, not spurting
Isn't it that...? (introduces a suggested reading)
A refutation that disproves an אמורא's view

phrases.english: They raised an objection: What is the blood of bloodletting
with which the soul departs?
As long as it is spurting.
This excludes the blood of exudate,
because it merely flows.
What, is it not that even the first and last [blood],
since it flows –
is considered like blood of exudate?
This is a refutation of Reish Lakish!

steps.triggerLanguage: מיתיבי איזהו דם הקזה שהנשמה יוצאה בו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks ריש לקיש's position from Step 18.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's view that red blood counts even before and after the spurt.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא excludes blood because 'it only flows.' The first and last red blood also only flows, so it should be excluded too, against ריש לקיש.

steps.title: The ברייתא only excludes the black blood
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא excludes only the black blood. The first and last red blood counts as life-blood even though it only flows.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. It comes to exclude the black blood. But the first and last blood, even though it only flows, is life-blood.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends ריש לקיש by reading the ברייתא's exclusion more narrowly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא says the ברייתא is not ruling out all blood that flows. It is only ruling out the black blood. The first and last red blood, even though it does not spurt, is still דם הנפש, just as ריש לקיש said.

keyTerms.meaning: To exclude, to leave out
The blackish blood
Even though
Life-blood, blood that carries כרת

steps.whatToRemember: ריש לקיש survives: the black blood is excluded, but all red blood, whether it spurts or just flows, is life-blood according to him.

phrases.english: No, it is to exclude the black blood;
but the first and last blood,
even though it flows –
this is blood of the soul.

steps.triggerLanguage: לא למעוטי דם המשחיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 19 by rereading the ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the ברייתא's exclusion (reinterpreting what it comes to exclude)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא excludes all blood that only flows, including the first and last red blood.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא excludes only the black blood. The first and last red blood is still life-blood, so ריש לקיש stands.

steps.title: A second ברייתא seems to refute ריש לקיש
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says that only spurting blood counts. It clearly leaves out the first and last blood because that blood only trickles. This looks like a full refutation of ריש לקיש.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged: Which is the 'first blood' that counts? All the time that it spurts. The first and last blood are left out, because that blood only trickles. This is a refutation of ריש לקיש!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא to attack ריש לקיש again. This one openly says that the first and last blood do not count.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 20 the גמרא answered the first ברייתא by saying it only left out the black blood. This new ברייתא names the first and last blood directly, so that answer no longer works. Only blood that spurts counts here, which fits רבי יוחנן and goes against ריש לקיש.

keyTerms.meaning: Spurting, gushing out with force
Trickling, flowing out slowly
Here: the main blood that counts as life-blood
A full refutation, a strong attack with no easy answer

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up 'first blood' (דָּם רִאשׁוֹן, the main life-blood) with 'the first and last' blood (רִאשׁוֹן וְאַחֲרוֹן, the weak trickles at the start and end). The ברייתא counts the first and leaves out the second.

phrases.english: They challenged: Which is the 'first blood'?
phrases.notes: 'First blood' here means the main blood that counts as life-blood, not the first drops to come out.

phrases.english: All the time that it spurts.
The first and last blood are left out,
because it only trickles.
This is a refutation of ריש לקיש!

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵיתִיבִי: אֵיזֶהוּ דָּם רִאשׁוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Renews the attack on ריש לקיש with a ברייתא that the answer in step 20 cannot handle
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's view that blood counts from right after the black drops, even when it only trickles
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא names the first and last trickling blood and leaves it out, so ריש לקיש's view seems to clash with a ברייתא

steps.title: ריש לקיש answers that this is an argument among תנאים
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש can say this ברייתא follows one תנא only. Another ברייתא shows that רבי אלעזר requires spurting blood, while רבי שמעון counts blood from the black drop onward. ריש לקיש follows רבי שמעון.
steps.simpleTranslation: He can tell you: it is an argument among תנאים. As it was taught: Which is the life-blood? All the time that it spurts. This is the view of רבי אלעזר. רבי שמעון says: from the black drop onward.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends ריש לקיש. He does not need to agree with that ברייתא, because תנאים already argue about this exact point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא from step 21 matches רבי אלעזר, who counts only spurting blood. רבי שמעון counts everything from the black drop onward, even blood that trickles. So רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש are just repeating an older argument, and ריש לקיש is not refuted.

keyTerms.meaning: It is an argument among תנאים, so an אמורא may follow either side
Life-blood, the blood the soul leaves with, which brings liability
The black, dark drop that comes out at the start
And onward, from that point on

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן = רבי אלעזר (only spurting blood counts). ריש לקיש = רבי שמעון (from the black drop onward, even if it trickles).

phrases.english: He can tell you: it is an argument among תנאים,
phrases.notes: 'He' is ריש לקיש. The גמרא speaks for him.

phrases.english: as it was taught: Which is the life-blood?
All the time that it spurts,
this is the view of רבי אלעזר.
רבי שמעון says:
From the black drop and onward.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָךְ: תַּנָּאֵי הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 21 by showing it matches only one side of an argument among תנאים
steps.terutzResolutionType: Dispute among תנאים: the challenging ברייתא follows one תנא, and ריש לקיש follows the other
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to be the only view, so ריש לקיש looked refuted
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is רבי אלעזר's view. ריש לקיש follows רבי שמעון, who counts blood from the black drop onward

steps.title: Spurting blood does not make seeds able to become impure
steps.stepSummary: The school of רבי ישמעאל learns from a פסוק that spurting blood is left out. It does not make seeds able to receive טומאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of רבי ישמעאל taught: 'And drinks the blood of the slain.' This leaves out spurting blood, which does not make seeds able to receive טומאה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a related teaching about spurting blood, from a different area of הלכה. This is a side point, not part of the argument above.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Some liquids make food 'ready' to become impure (הכשר). The פסוק speaks of the blood of the 'slain', meaning dead, so only that blood counts as a liquid for this purpose. Spurting blood, which leaves while the animal is still alive, is left out.

keyTerms.meaning: Blood of the slain, blood of those already dead
To leave out, to exclude
Makes food able to become impure (הֶכְשֵׁר)
Seeds, produce

steps.confusionAlert: This is about טומאה (making seeds able to become impure), not about the איסור of eating blood. Spurting blood is the main blood for the איסור of eating, but it does not count for הכשר.

phrases.english: The school of רבי ישמעאל taught:
'And drinks the blood of the slain',
to leave out spurting blood,
which does not make seeds able to receive טומאה.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנָא דְּבֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A related side teaching that uses the same idea of spurting blood, but in the area of טומאה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Spurting blood from slaughter is not counted as a liquid that makes seeds able to receive טומאה

steps.title: רבי ירמיה asks about blood caught in two cups
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה asks רבי זירא: if someone let blood from an animal into two cups and drank them, he is surely liable for the first cup. Is he also liable for the second cup?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה asked רבי זירא: If someone let blood from an animal and caught its blood in two cups, what is the law? For the first cup, everyone agrees he is liable. For the last cup, is he liable or not?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the איסור of eating blood with a new question. רבי ירמיה asks about blood that comes out in two stages.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first cup has the strong, spurting blood, so everyone agrees it is life-blood. The second cup has the weaker blood that comes out afterward. The question is whether that later blood also brings liability.

keyTerms.meaning: Let blood, cut a vein to drain blood
Cups
Everyone agrees
What is the law?

phrases.aramaic: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה מֵרַבִּי זֵירָא:
phrases.english: רבי ירמיה asked רבי זירא:
If someone let blood from an animal
and caught its blood in two cups, what is the law?
For the first cup, everyone agrees he is liable,

phrases.aramaic: עַל הָאַחֲרוֹן – מִי מִיחַיַּיב אוֹ לָא?
phrases.english: for the last cup, is he liable or not?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה מֵרַבִּי זֵירָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back from the side point about טומאה to the איסור of eating blood, using a practical case
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the blood in the second cup, which comes after the spurting, also brings liability

steps.title: רבי זירא: this is the argument of רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא answers that this exact case is an argument. ריש לקיש says he must bring two חטאות. רבי יוחנן says he must bring only one.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: This is the argument of רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש, as it was said: If someone let blood from an animal and caught its blood in two cups, ריש לקיש says he is liable to bring two חטאות. רבי יוחנן says he is liable to bring only one.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא answers that this question was already argued by רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This matches their views from step 18. ריש לקיש counts the later blood too, so drinking each cup in a separate lapse of awareness needs its own חטאת. רבי יוחנן counts only spurting blood, so only the first cup brings liability.

keyTerms.meaning: An argument, a dispute
A sin-offering brought for doing an איסור by mistake
Two sin-offerings

steps.whatToRemember: Two cups of blood: ריש לקיש says both cups count, so two חטאות. רבי יוחנן says only the first cup counts, so one חטאת.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows the practical result of the argument from step 18. It decides whether the later, weaker blood brings a separate חטאת.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: פְּלוּגְתָּא דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן וְרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ,
phrases.english: He said to him: This is the argument of רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש,
as it was said: If someone let blood from an animal
and caught its blood in two cups,

phrases.aramaic: רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ אָמַר: חַיָּיב שְׁתֵּי חַטָּאוֹת.
phrases.english: ריש לקיש says: he is liable to bring two sin-offerings.

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: אֵינוֹ חַיָּיב אֶלָּא אַחַת.
phrases.english: And רבי יוחנן says: he is liable to bring only one.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: פְּלוּגְתָּא דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן וְרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי ירמיה's question by pointing to an argument between אמוראים that already exists
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It depends on the argument: ריש לקיש says he is liable for the second cup too (two חטאות), and רבי יוחנן says only for the first cup (one חטאת)

steps.title: רבי יהודה makes one liable for oozing blood
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה rules that a person who eats דם התמצית is liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says a person is liable for eating the oozing blood.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the line in the משנה where רבי יהודה disagrees with the first opinion. He says eating דם התמצית does make a person liable. This sets up רבי אלעזר's comment in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion in the משנה says there is no liability for דם התמצית, the blood that oozes out after the strong spurt is over. רבי יהודה, in the same משנה, counts this blood too, so eating it makes a person liable.

keyTerms.meaning: Oozing blood that slowly drains out after the main spurt of blood stops
Holds a person liable

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda holds one liable for blood of exudate (oozing blood).

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה מְחַיֵּיב בְּדַם הַתַּמְצִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the two-cups question to a new opinion about oozing blood.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהודה, eating דם התמצית makes a person liable.

steps.title: Even רבי יהודה agrees oozing blood does not atone
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר says that רבי יהודה agrees דם התמצית does not bring כפרה, based on a פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: רבי יהודה agrees when it comes to atonement. The פסוק says, 'For it is the blood that atones by the soul.' Blood that the life leaves with atones. Blood that the life does not leave with does not atone.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר limits רבי יהודה's view. Oozing blood counts for liability, but it cannot be used for atonement on the מזבח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק ties כפרה to the blood 'with the soul', meaning the blood that comes out as the animal's life leaves it. That is the spurting blood. Oozing blood comes later, so even רבי יהודה agrees it does not atone.

keyTerms.meaning: Agrees (here: agrees on this point even though he argues elsewhere)
Atonement brought by the blood of a קרבן
The life goes out with it, meaning the spurting blood at the moment of death

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two questions. רבי יהודה makes a person liable for eating oozing blood, but he agrees that the same blood does not atone on the מזבח.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said:
Rabbi Yehuda agrees regarding atonement,
as it says: “For it is the blood that atones by the soul”
blood that the soul goes out with atones,

phrases.aramaic: וְשֶׁאֵין הַנֶּפֶשׁ יוֹצְאָה בּוֹ אֵינוֹ מְכַפֵּר.
phrases.english: and blood that the soul does not go out with does not atone.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: מוֹדֶה רַבִּי יְהוּדָה לְעִנְיַן כַּפָּרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits רבי יהודה's ruling from step 26 to liability only, not atonement.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only spurting blood atones. Even רבי יהודה agrees דם התמצית does not atone.

steps.title: A ברייתא in the ספרא proves רבי אלעזר right
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק brings a ברייתא showing that only spurting blood of קדשים atones, and that 'כל דם' is needed to include oozing blood. The ספרא follows רבי יהודה, so רבי יהודה agrees oozing blood does not atone.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: We also learned this in a ברייתא. Why does the פסוק say 'any blood' and not just 'blood'? Because from 'the blood atones by the soul' I would only know about blood of קדשים that spurts out with the life, since it atones. How do I know about blood of חולין and oozing blood? The פסוק says 'any blood.' Who wrote an unnamed ספרא? רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק supports רבי אלעזר with a ברייתא. It shows the same author counts oozing blood for liability but not for atonement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא needs the extra word 'כל' to include oozing blood in the איסור. That means the atonement פסוק alone does not cover oozing blood, so oozing blood does not atone. Since an unnamed ספרא is by רבי יהודה, this proves רבי יהודה holds both ideas, just as רבי אלעזר said.

keyTerms.meaning: We also learned this, introducing a source that backs up a statement
Why does the פסוק say this? It asks what an extra word teaches
Blood of animals brought as קרבנות
Blood of regular, non-holy animals
An unnamed teaching in the ספרא, the מדרש on ויקרא, assumed to follow רבי יהודה

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי יהודה, oozing blood is forbidden to eat (from 'כל דם') but cannot atone (from 'כי הדם הוא בנפש יכפר').

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
We also learned this, as it is taught in a ברייתא:
It could say “blood”; why does the verse say “any blood”?

phrases.aramaic: לְפִי שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״כִּי הַדָּם הוּא בַּנֶּפֶשׁ יְכַפֵּר״,
phrases.english: Since it says: “For it is the blood that atones by the soul,”
I would only know about blood of sacrifices
that the soul goes out with, since it atones,
From where do we know blood of non-holy animals and oozing blood?
The verse says: “Any blood.”

phrases.aramaic: סְתָם סִיפְרָא מַנִּי? רַבִּי יְהוּדָה הִיא.
phrases.english: Whose view is an unnamed Sifra? It is Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַף אֲנַן נָמֵי תְּנֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא to support רבי אלעזר's statement in step 27.
steps.raayaObject: רבי אלעזר's claim that רבי יהודה agrees oozing blood does not atone.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא in the ספרא, which follows רבי יהודה, needs 'כל דם' to include oozing blood. This shows the atonement פסוק does not include it.

steps.title: New משנה: a doubtful case of misusing holy property
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא says a person unsure whether he did מעילה brings an אשם תלוי, and the חכמים exempt him. רבי עקיבא agrees he does not pay for the מעילה until he knows for sure, because then he brings a definite אשם along with it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא holds a person liable to bring an אשם תלוי for a doubt of מעילה, and the חכמים exempt him. רבי עקיבא agrees that he does not bring the payment for his מעילה until he finds out for sure, so that he can bring a definite אשם together with it.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It argues about whether an אשם תלוי is brought when a person is unsure if he did מעילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually an אשם תלוי is brought when a person is unsure whether he did a sin that needs a חטאת. מעילה needs an אשם, not a חטאת, so the חכמים say no אשם תלוי. רבי עקיבא requires one anyway. He still agrees the payment for the מעילה waits until the person knows for sure, because it goes together with a definite אשם.

keyTerms.meaning: Using holy property (הקדש) for personal benefit
Doubt, when a person is not sure whether he sinned
A 'hanging' guilt offering, brought when a person is not sure whether he sinned
Exempt, they do not require it
A definite guilt offering, brought when the sin is known for sure

steps.whyThisMatters: This opens a new topic: whether an אשם תלוי applies to sins that bring an אשם, not only to sins that bring a חטאת.

phrases.english: MISHNA:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא מְחַיֵּיב עַל סְפֵק מְעִילָה אָשָׁם תָּלוּי,
phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva holds one liable to bring a provisional guilt offering for a doubt of misusing holy property,
and the Sages exempt him.

phrases.aramaic: וּמוֹדֶה רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא שֶׁאֵינוֹ מֵבִיא אֶת מְעִילָתוֹ
phrases.english: And Rabbi Akiva agrees that he does not bring payment for his misuse
until it becomes known to him for sure,
so that he brings a definite guilt offering along with it.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא מְחַיֵּיב עַל סְפֵק מְעִילָה אָשָׁם תָּלוּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on a new topic after the blood discussion ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי עקיבא requires an אשם תלוי for a doubt of מעילה and the חכמים exempt. רבי עקיבא concedes that the payment for מעילה waits until the sin is known for sure, when it is brought with a definite אשם.

steps.title: רבי טרפון's one-offering plan
steps.stepSummary: רבי טרפון suggests that the person pay the מעילה and חומש right away, together with one conditional אשם, so he never needs two offerings.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי טרפון said: Why should this person bring two guilt offerings? Instead, he should pay the misuse money and its extra fifth, and bring one guilt offering worth two סלעים, and say: 'If I really did misuse, this is my misuse payment and this is my guilt offering. If it is only a doubt, the money is a donation and the offering is an אשם תלוי.' This works because the same kind of animal is brought whether the sin is known or not known.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי טרפון pushes back on bringing an אשם תלוי now and a definite אשם later. He offers a simpler plan that uses one conditional offering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under רבי עקיבא's view, the person brings an אשם תלוי now, and if he later finds out he sinned, he brings a definite אשם along with the payment. רבי טרפון says to do everything at once, using conditions. If he sinned, the money pays his debt and the animal is his definite אשם. If he did not sin, the money becomes a donation and the animal counts as an אשם תלוי. This works because both kinds of אשם use the same animal, a ram worth two סלעים.

keyTerms.meaning: Using הקדש (Temple-owned property) for personal benefit
The extra fifth added to the payment for מעילה
A provisional guilt offering brought when one is unsure whether he sinned
A voluntary donation to the Temple
סלעים, coins; an אשם must be worth at least two of them
"It became known": the case where the person knows for sure he sinned

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a single conditional act can cover both possible situations, so one offering does the job of two.

phrases.english: Rabbi Tarfon said:
Why should this person bring two guilt offerings?
phrases.notes: The two are the אשם תלוי now and the definite אשם later, as in רבי עקיבא's view in the previous step.

phrases.english: Rather, he brings the misuse payment and its fifth,
and he brings a guilt offering worth two sela,
and he says:
"If I certainly misused,
this is my misuse payment and this is my guilt offering;
and if it is doubtful whether I misused,
the money is a donation,
and the guilt offering is a provisional one."
For from the same type that he brings for a known sin,
he brings for an unknown one.
phrases.notes: Both a definite אשם and an אשם תלוי are a ram worth two סלעים, so one animal can serve either role.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי טַרְפוֹן: מָה לָזֶה מֵבִיא שְׁתֵּי אֲשָׁמוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to רבי עקיבא's position in step 29, which leads to two separate offerings, by proposing a single conditional one.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Pay the מעילה and חומש now and bring one conditional אשם. If he did not sin, the money is a donation and the animal is an אשם תלוי.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: the plan only fits small amounts
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא says רבי טרפון's plan makes sense for a small מעילה. For a huge amount, it is better to bring only the cheap אשם תלוי and not pay the big sum on a doubt.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא said: His words make sense for a small misuse. But if a person has a doubt about misusing a hundred מנה, isn't it better for him to bring a guilt offering worth two סלעים than to pay a hundred מנה for a misuse that might never have happened?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא partly rejects רבי טרפון's plan. He shows that it can be very costly when the amount in doubt is large.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under רבי טרפון's plan, the person pays the full מעילה amount plus the fifth up front, even though he may not owe it. If the amount is tiny, that is no big loss. If it is a hundred מנה, paying it all on a doubt is a heavy loss, while an אשם תלוי costs only two סלעים. So רבי עקיבא's approach of bringing the אשם תלוי now and paying only once he knows for sure protects the person's money.

keyTerms.meaning: A small, low-value מעילה
A case where one is unsure whether he did מעילה
A large coin worth one hundred דינרים

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva said:
His words seem right for a small misuse.
But if there comes to his hand
a doubtful misuse worth a hundred maneh,
is it not better for him that he bring
a guilt offering worth two sela,

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא יָבִיא סְפֵק מְעִילָה בְּמֵאָה מָנֶה?
phrases.english: and not bring payment for a doubtful misuse of a hundred maneh?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא: נִרְאִין דְּבָרָיו בִּמְעִילָה מְעוּטָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits רבי טרפון's plan from step 30 by pointing out its cost when the amount is large.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Partial: the plan is rejected only for large amounts and accepted for small ones.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Paying a large מעילה amount on a mere doubt risks a big, needless loss, while an אשם תלוי costs only two סלעים.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא agrees for a small misuse
steps.stepSummary: The משנה concludes that רבי עקיבא agrees with רבי טרפון's plan when the amount of מעילה is small.
steps.simpleTranslation: So רבי עקיבא agrees with רבי טרפון when the misuse is small.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה sums up the result of the exchange: the two sages agree when the amount is small.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The disagreement is now narrowed. For a small amount, both sages accept paying up front and bringing one conditional אשם. They differ only when a large sum is at stake.

keyTerms.meaning: Agrees, concedes

steps.whatToRemember: רבי טרפון: pay the מעילה and חומש now and bring one conditional אשם. רבי עקיבא accepts this only for a small amount. For a large amount, bring just the אשם תלוי and pay later if the sin is confirmed.
steps.confusionAlert: רבי עקיבא does not fully accept רבי טרפון's view. He agrees only for small amounts. For large amounts, he still holds that one should not pay on a doubt.

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva agrees with Rabbi Tarfon
regarding a small misuse.

steps.triggerLanguage: מוֹדֶה רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא לְרַבִּי טַרְפוֹן בִּמְעִילָה מְעוּטָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the bottom line from רבי עקיבא's response in step 31.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: For a small מעילה, רבי עקיבא agrees that one pays up front and brings one conditional אשם, following רבי טרפון.
